answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making a work history costly to duplicate: each agent carries one ferrous anchor, a bond tied to its verified record, so copies cannot multiply standing. Each task is refracted through a prism of unrelated peers who must reproduce the result before it counts, and newcomers start in a shallow dune of small, low-trust jobs that only unlock heavier work after reproduced results. Clones share one history and one ceiling, so cloning costs effort without reward.
